method: time-constrained visual encounter surveys of 30 minutes each hour (14 times per day) between 6:00 am and 8:00 pm; activity rate taken as the number of active individuals found
conditions: Free-living adult lizards in a coastal sand-dune remnant (restinga) at Grussaí, Rio de Janeiro state, Brazil, 14 days in December 2010 and 15 days in January 2011 (austral summer only; no other season and no night sampling). Activity started around 6:00 am and ended before 7:00 pm; the paper contrasts this bimodal pattern with an unimodal pattern and a shorter activity window (about 7:00 am to 5:00 pm) reported for other populations of the species. Lizards were collected manually or with an air-pressured gun to take body temperature (29 lizards collected per the Results; the Methods do not say whether they were released), so the survey counts are field observations and the animals were not captive. No bait or lure.

source.authors: Maia-Carneiro T, Winck GR, Pereira MR, Rocha CFD
source.title: Body orientation for thermoregulation and daily activity cycle of Mabuya macrorhyncha (Squamata: Scincidae)

quote: The activity cycle of the lizards was bimodal, with the first peak between 6:00 and 11:00 am and the second from 2:00 to 7:00 pm.
